profile.focus: つなぐにほんご 初級1, the classroom course: one stone per textbook lesson, one app lesson per part
profile.kanji: Kana only in Lessons 1–5, as the book prints them; the book’s kanji from Lesson 6, with furigana.

levels.name: Lessons 1–5
levels.goal: Greet, shop, get around, talk about the day and eat out, in polite Japanese written in kana.

levels.name: Lessons 6–8
levels.goal: Adjectives, plans and the first kanji; casual talk with friends.

levels.name: Lessons 9–10
levels.goal: The て form: instructions, rules and states; introducing people and places.

levels.name: Lessons 11–15
levels.goal: Thanks, requests, invitations, advice and apologies.

nodes.title: First Greetings
nodes.summary: Meet people at a party, greet the neighbours and say where you come from.
outcomes: Greet someone you meet for the first time and give your name.
Ask and say someone’s country and work.
Greet neighbours at different times of day.
Make small talk about the weather, and ask someone to say it again or more slowly.
Greet the neighbours you will rely on when you move in.
Ask and say when and from where someone came.

stages.title: First Greetings
stages.focus: Meet people, greet the neighbours and say where you come from.

expansions.title: Practices and books
expansions.scope: Countries and jobs, numbers to 100, phone numbers and months, and the interview-and-introduce activity; a book for each part, the last one three self-introductions.
expansions.readiness: Finish the part each practice or book is homed at.

nodes.capstone: Interview a classmate about their name, country and work, then introduce them to the group (the アクティビティー).
nodes.transfer: Out Shopping opens with これ, which New Next Door meets when handing over a gift; every later stone starts with these greetings.

nodes.title: Out Shopping
nodes.summary: Order at a counter by price and number, find departments and goods in a department store, and ask for another colour or size.
outcomes: Tell the clerk what you want and how many, and ask the price.
Point things out with これ, それ and あれ, and with この, その and あの before a noun.
Ask where a department is and which floor it is on.
Ask where goods are, and follow となり, まえ and うしろ.
Ask whether the shop has another colour or size, and say what is wrong with it.
Leave a shop politely without buying.

stages.title: Out Shopping
stages.focus: Buy things at a counter, find your way round a department store and ask for another colour or size.

expansions.title: Practices and books
expansions.scope: Prices to 10,000 and counting to ten, store floors, more adjectives and いい, and the compare-prices activity; a book for each part, and a department-store sale flyer after the よみましょう.
expansions.readiness: Finish the part each practice or book is homed at.

nodes.capstone: Compare the prices of eggs, toilet paper and taxis across countries and present them (the アクティビティー); find each shopper’s floor and price on a sale flyer (よみましょう).
nodes.transfer: Trains and Buses reuses prices and どこですか on the way to the station, where these こ・そ・あ words become places: ここ, そこ, あそこ.

nodes.title: Trains and Buses
nodes.summary: Say how you get somewhere and what you want to do, find a bus stop and the next bus, and ask the fare, the time and the platform at a station.
outcomes: Ask and say how you get somewhere: by train, by bus or on foot.
Say what you want or don’t want to do with ～たいです.
Ask where a bus stop, a station or a shop is, and say what is near.
Ask the time, when the next bus comes and which number bus to take.
Ask how long a trip takes, and the fare and the platform.
Say where you are, and ask whether someone is there.

stages.title: Trains and Buses
stages.focus: Get around town by train and bus: how to go, when the bus comes, the fare and the platform.

expansions.title: Practices and books
expansions.scope: Places in town and who you go with; clock times, days and rooms; fares, travel times and who is where; and the plan-a-route activity. A book for each part, and a departure board after the よみましょう.
expansions.readiness: Finish the part each practice or book is homed at.

nodes.capstone: Plan a trip on a simple rail map, note where, how and how much, and present the route (the アクティビティー); then find the next train and its platform on a departure board (よみましょう).
nodes.transfer: Day to Day builds daily routines on the clock times and ～から ～まで from this stone, and Eating Out returns to ～たいです when ordering a meal.

nodes.title: Day to Day
nodes.summary: Tell the teacher about your mornings, talk about lunch at the office, and share the work of cooking together.
outcomes: Talk about your daily life: what you do and where.
Say at what time you do things, and from when to when.
Say what you did and did not do.
Ask and say who did something, and whose something is.
Say what you will do when working with others.
Ask and say where a tool or other thing is.

stages.title: Day to Day
stages.focus: Talk about your day, what you did and the work you share with others.

expansions.title: Practices and books
expansions.scope: How often and with whom, the past week, and where things are; the アクティビティー becomes a survey of classmates’ days; a book for each part, the last an email exchange after the よみましょう.
expansions.readiness: Finish the part each practice or book is homed at.

nodes.capstone: Read a classmate’s timetable, narrate their day from tiles and ask follow-up questions (the アクティビティー); read an email exchange planning a weekend (よみましょう).
nodes.transfer: Eating Out invites people out with ～ませんか and uses the past tense from Do You Cook? to talk about meals.

nodes.title: Eating Out
nodes.summary: Invite friends out to eat, get a table, order from a menu and talk about how the food tastes.
outcomes: Invite someone to eat or drink, and accept or turn down an invitation.
Tell the restaurant staff how many you are and which seats you want.
Talk about what to order from a menu, and decide with ～に します.
Ask what something on the menu is.
Say how food tastes, including what it is not, and add a “but”.
Say what you want.

stages.title: Eating Out
stages.focus: Invite friends out, get a table, order from a menu and talk about the food.

expansions.title: Practices and books
expansions.scope: Planning a meal with ～ましょうか, ordering from a menu, taste words with ～たいです and そして, and the plan-a-meal-out activity; a book for each part, the last one a café menu flyer.
expansions.readiness: Finish the part each practice or book is homed at.

nodes.capstone: Plan a meal out with friends: invite them, get a table, order and talk about the food, then tell the group the plan (the アクティビティー); read a café menu flyer and an order (よみましょう).
nodes.transfer: Plans and Trips turns the taste words into past and negative adjectives and talks about plans and what you did; invitations come back in Invitations.

nodes.title: Plans and Trips
nodes.summary: Talk about holiday plans, what a place is like and how a trip went.
outcomes: Ask and answer about holiday plans, and give a simple reason.
Ask and say what a travel spot is like, and introduce its specialities.
Ask and say what someone did on a trip, and ask and give impressions.

stages.title: Plans and Trips
stages.focus: Talk about holiday plans, what a place is like and how a trip went.

expansions.title: Practices and books
expansions.scope: One general practice and one general book per part; the アクティビティー becomes a practice on the last part, and the よみましょう a book.
expansions.readiness: Finish the part the practice or book is homed at.

nodes.capstone: Talk about sights you want to visit and give a short talk about a place you went (the アクティビティー); read a diary of a trip (よみましょう).
nodes.transfer: The first kanji arrive here; Among Friends starts casual speech.

nodes.title: Among Friends
nodes.summary: Chat casually with friends about weekend plans, joining in and things you don’t know.
outcomes: Talk about weekend plans with a teacher, and with friends.
Tell a teacher, and a friend, whether you will join a weekend event.
Ask a teacher or a friend about something you don’t know, and say how you feel.

stages.title: Among Friends
stages.focus: Chat casually with friends about weekend plans, joining in and things you don’t know.

expansions.title: Practices and books
expansions.scope: One general practice and one general book per part; the アクティビティー becomes a practice on the last part, and the よみましょう a book.
expansions.readiness: Finish the part the practice or book is homed at.

nodes.capstone: Ask polite question cards casually, inviting a friend to a film (the アクティビティー); read survey charts on foreign friends (よみましょう).
nodes.transfer: Catching Up adds the た form for casual talk about the past.

nodes.title: Catching Up
nodes.summary: Tell friends what you did and how it went, in casual speech.
outcomes: Ask and tell friends what they did at the weekend.
Talk with friends about what you did on a day off and how it was.
Report politely to a group what you talked about casually.

stages.title: Catching Up
stages.focus: Tell friends what you did and how it went, in casual speech.

expansions.title: Practices and books
expansions.scope: One general practice and one general book per part; the アクティビティー becomes a practice on the last part, and the よみましょう a book.
expansions.readiness: Finish the part the practice or book is homed at.

nodes.capstone: Talk casually about a match and the holidays, then report to the group politely (the アクティビティー); read a casual email about a trip (よみましょう).
nodes.transfer: Rules and Instructions returns to polite speech with the て form.

nodes.title: Rules and Instructions
nodes.summary: Follow rules and instructions at school and at work, and say what you are doing.
outcomes: Understand rubbish-disposal instructions, apologise for a mistake and ask the landlord about the rules.
Understand test instructions, and ask a teacher or the person in charge what is allowed.
Understand a teacher’s instructions, and say what others are doing.

stages.title: Rules and Instructions
stages.focus: Follow rules and instructions at school and at work, and say what you are doing.

expansions.title: Practices and books
expansions.scope: One general practice and one general book per part; the アクティビティー becomes a practice on the last part, and the よみましょう a book.
expansions.readiness: Finish the part the practice or book is homed at.

nodes.capstone: Explain signs and marks, then design and present your own sign (the アクティビティー); match short rule lists to places (よみましょう).
nodes.transfer: People and Places uses ～て います for clothes and states.

nodes.title: People and Places
nodes.summary: Point people out, say where you live and describe your town.
outcomes: Ask and say who someone is from their clothes or actions, and introduce someone.
Introduce family and friends, and ask and say where someone lives, their job and whether they are married.
Introduce your town simply, and say how you feel about something.

stages.title: People and Places
stages.focus: Point people out, say where you live and describe your town.

expansions.title: Practices and books
expansions.scope: One general practice and one general book per part; the アクティビティー becomes a practice on the last part, and the よみましょう a book.
expansions.readiness: Finish the part the practice or book is homed at.

nodes.capstone: Introduce a friend for a part-time job from a profile card (the アクティビティー); guess jobs from two first-person texts (よみましょう).
nodes.transfer: Saying Thanks moves to giving and receiving.

nodes.title: Saying Thanks
nodes.summary: Thank people for gifts and help, and say who did what for you.
outcomes: Discuss what to give as a present, and thank someone for a present.
Thank someone for a compliment, and explain who gave or made something for you and when.
Offer help to someone in trouble, and thank someone for their help.

stages.title: Saying Thanks
stages.focus: Thank people for gifts and help, and say who did what for you.

expansions.title: Practices and books
expansions.scope: One general practice and one general book per part; the アクティビティー becomes a practice on the last part, and the よみましょう a book.
expansions.readiness: Finish the part the practice or book is homed at.

nodes.capstone: Thank a boss after a meal and choose what to say in four situations (the アクティビティー); read a story of being helped abroad (よみましょう).
nodes.transfer: Asking a Favour turns the て form into requests.

nodes.title: Asking a Favour
nodes.summary: Ask for help, politely or casually, and ask for permission.
outcomes: Give a reason and make a simple request, and ask about and follow a simple procedure.
Give a reason and make a polite request, and explain a problem and ask for help.
Make a simple request to a friend, and ask a friend for something awkward.
Say you feel unwell and leave early or take time off, giving a reason and getting permission.

stages.title: Asking a Favour
stages.focus: Ask for help, politely or casually, and ask for permission.

expansions.title: Practices and books
expansions.scope: One general practice and one general book per part; the アクティビティー becomes a practice on the last part, and the よみましょう a book.
expansions.readiness: Finish the part the practice or book is homed at.

nodes.capstone: Role-play asking for help in four situations (the アクティビティー); read a university test notice (よみましょう).
nodes.transfer: Invitations moves on to inviting people.

nodes.title: Invitations
nodes.summary: Invite people, and accept or turn down an invitation politely.
outcomes: Invite a coworker for a meal, accept and discuss where to go.
Invite a coworker to go out, and settle the date when invited.
Invite a friend to an event, and turn down a friend’s invitation.

stages.title: Invitations
stages.focus: Invite people, and accept or turn down an invitation politely.

expansions.title: Practices and books
expansions.scope: One general practice and one general book per part; the アクティビティー becomes a practice on the last part, and the よみましょう a book.
expansions.readiness: Finish the part the practice or book is homed at.

nodes.capstone: Give a recruiting pitch for a university club (the アクティビティー); read a volunteer-recruitment poster (よみましょう).
nodes.transfer: Good Advice moves on to giving advice.

nodes.title: Good Advice
nodes.summary: Give advice and suggestions for everyday problems.
outcomes: Speak to someone who looks unwell, and give simple advice.
Pass on information that helps solve a problem, and say what you can and cannot do.
Ask whether someone has been somewhere, and explain, advise and suggest about a destination.

stages.title: Good Advice
stages.focus: Give advice and suggestions for everyday problems.
lessons: Why Not Give It a Go?

expansions.title: Practices and books
expansions.scope: One general practice and one general book per part; the アクティビティー becomes a practice on the last part, and the よみましょう a book.
expansions.readiness: Finish the part the practice or book is homed at.

nodes.capstone: Advise a student struggling with kanji, then share a problem and advise each other (the アクティビティー); read a newspaper article on a new hospital (よみましょう).
nodes.transfer: Saying Sorry closes the course with apologies.

nodes.title: Saying Sorry
nodes.summary: Apologise for mistakes, politely and to friends.
outcomes: Apologise politely for something you did.
Explain simply what happened.
Apologise to a friend, and explain to a friend what happened.

stages.title: Saying Sorry
stages.focus: Apologise for mistakes, politely and to friends.

expansions.title: Practices and books
expansions.scope: One general practice and one general book per part; the アクティビティー becomes a practice on the last part, and the よみましょう a book.
expansions.readiness: Finish the part the practice or book is homed at.

nodes.capstone: Say what you would do after a mistake in several situations (the アクティビティー); read an apology email for a lost book (よみましょう).
nodes.transfer: The last stone of this book; the next book carries on from here.

sources.use: The course book: lesson order, parts, scenes, patterns and script; with the school’s handout, the vocabulary of each part. Niwa’s dialogues, drills and readings are newly written.

sources.title: みんなの日本語 初級 Translation & Grammar Notes
